lesson_title: Socks and Shoes: Running the Rule Backwards
hook_text: A machine does times 3, then plus 2. Out comes 20. What went in? Most people divide first. Most people are wrong.
clip_script: Picture a machine with two gears: times 3, then plus 2. Drop in 4: 12, then 14. Now the hard way round. Out comes 20 — what went in? Think socks and shoes. Socks first, shoes second. To undo, shoes come off FIRST. So undo the last gear first: 20 minus 2 is 18. Then undo times 3: 18 over 3 is 6. Six went in. Check: 6, 18, 20. Divide first instead and you get 4,666... an ugly number, and ugly means wrong order. One more trap: a squaring gear. Square, then minus 1, out comes 24. Undo the minus: 25. What squares to 25? Five AND negative five. Two answers, give both. Every equation you solve is a machine run backwards.
visual_style: A cartoon machine with two labelled gears; a number drops in and transforms through each gear; then the film runs in reverse with the gears glowing in the opposite order, a sock and a shoe icon flashing beside them.
pacing: Steady forward run, a snap reverse, a pause on the two-answer twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run any rule backwards without fear.
